cases.reason: The FD formats 1-3 are the same in 13.3.4.1 and 13.4.5.2 phrase by phrase. 2002 shows the LINAGE clause inline, 2023 names it linage-clause; the phrases are the same. 2023 adds SR4 (LINE SEQUENTIAL), which is a separate rule. No CD reach: an FD is not a CD. No obsolete or removed clause sits in a 2002 FD, so the 'clauses that follow' are the same set.

cases.reason: Format 2 is the same in both editions (EXTERNAL, GLOBAL, BLOCK, record-clause). The rule covers only the relative or indexed FD and the record entries associated with it. It refers to no other rule and has no communication or debugging reach.

citations.quote: For an indexed file, one or more record description entries shall be associated with the file description entry

cases.reason: The SD format holds only the RECORD clause in both editions: inline in 2002, record-clause in 2023. The rule asks only that an SD have record entries and refers to nothing else. No CD reach.

citations.quote: One or more record description entries shall be associated with the sort-merge file description entry
One or more record description entries shall be associated with the sort-merge file description entry

cases.reason: The procedure-division-header and the using-phrase are the same in both editions. SR1 and SR5 confine data-name-1 and data-name-2 to level 01 or 77 linkage entries in both, so a communication item cannot be either name. The rule is self-contained.

citations.quote: Data-name-2 shall not be the same as data-name-1
Data-name-2 shall be defined as a level 01 entry or level 77 entry in the linkage section

cases.reason: The RAISING phrase has the same three alternatives in both editions; 2023 renames class-name-1 to object-class-name-1. The interface-name-1 alternative is the same, and the REPOSITORY interface specifier is the same. The procedure division header cannot hold a communication or removed form.

citations.quote: Interface-name-1 shall be the name of an interface specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph
Interface-name-1 shall be the name of an interface specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph

cases.reason: The formats are the same (ROUNDED became rounded-phrase), but SR1 tests the category of identifier-1 and identifier-2. In 2002 either one may reference a communication-section item whose category comes only from Annex A: the implicit CD data-names (output CD: DESTINATION COUNT and TEXT LENGTH are unsigned integers, so legal; STATUS KEY and SYMBOLIC DESTINATION are alphanumeric, so illegal) and items of a user record under a CD (A.1.1.2). Annex A names 8.4.2.1 Identifier among its communication entities. 2023 has no CD, so its row witnesses neither leg. This is the same reach the p-18 refuter overturned for COMPUTE SR1 and CANCEL SR1. The reader probed both legs at 2002, and I re-ran them: refute-p-14/cd-ops.cob (DIVIDE 2 INTO TL, DIVIDE DC INTO 17, DIVIDE TL BY DC) prints TL=0008 Q=0008 R=0001 E=   4. refute-p-14/cd-ops-div-sk.cob (DIVIDE ... INTO SK) is refused with COBOL1675 'of category Alphanumeric'. Compiler at 2002: correct. Needs: its own 2002 verdict from these probes.

cases.reason: This is the same reach as SR1, for GIVING identifier-3 and REMAINDER identifier-4. Probes at 2002 (reader's, re-run by me): refute-p-14/cd-ops.cob (GIVING E, where the divisor DC and dividend TL are CD items) runs. refute-p-14/cd-ops-div-rem-sd.cob (REMAINDER SD1) is refused with COBOL1675 'of category Alphanumeric ... cases.reason: The formats are the same. Literal-1 and literal-2 are literals, which cannot be communication items. 2002's set of numeric literals is no wider than 2023's for an integer or fixed-point operand. The floating-point literal bounds (31/3 in 2002, 36/4 in 2023) that p-15 overturned on make 2002 narrower, and here that changes only which lexemes are numeric literals at all, which 8.3 decides. The rule itself is self-contained.

citations.quote: Literal-1 and literal-2 shall be numeric literals

cases.reason: The EVALUATE format, selection-subject, selection-object and range-expression are the same in both editions. A word-equivalence rule has no operand reach.

cases.reason: The format is the same. The rule counts selection objects, and a count does not depend on what an operand is or where it is defined.

cases.reason: The range-expression and the alphabet-name clause (12.2.6.1 against 12.3.7) are the same, but SR3 tests the class of identifier-3 and identifier-4. In 2002 these may be implicit CD data-names whose class comes only from Annex A: SYMBOLIC DESTINATION and STATUS KEY are alphanumeric, so IN alphabet-name-1 is permitted; TEXT LENGTH and DESTINATION COUNT are numeric, so it is forbidden. This is the same communication reach as DIVIDE SR1 and p-18's CANCEL SR1, and the 2023 row has no such items. My probes at 2002: refute-p-14/eval-cd-ok.cob (WHEN SD1 THRU SK IN ALPHA1) compiles and prints IN-RANGE. refute-p-14/eval-cd-num.cob (WHEN TL THRU DC IN ALPHA1) is refused with COBOL1998 'may be specified only when the operands of the THROUGH phrase are of class alphabetic, alphanumeric or national'. Compiler at 2002: correct.

cases.reason: 2002 format 6 is the same as 2023 format 4. The rule is banded FORMAT 6, so the removed EXIT METHOD and EXIT FUNCTION formats are not in its reach. cases.reason: Format 2 (historic) is the same, and NEXT SENTENCE is archaic in both editions. The permission depends only on where the ELSE NEXT SENTENCE phrase sits relative to the period, not on what statement-1 holds, so 2002-only statements inside statement-1 do not change it.

cases.reason: The reader found the reach and called it SAME on the strength of a probe. The rule tests the data description entry that identifier-1 references. In 2002 that entry may be a 66-level RENAMES entry following a record under a CD: user record entries redefine the CD area (A.1.1.2), and 2002 RENAMES SR3 names the CD as a qualifier of a RENAMES entry. 2023 RENAMES SR3 names only level 01, FD and SD. This is the class (a) cause, a data-description entry under a CD, and the 2023 row (pb416, pb966) cannot witness it. My re-run at 2002: refute-p-14/cd-init-66.cob (66 AB RENAMES A1 THRU B1 after a CD record; INITIALIZE AB) is refused with COBOL0835. Compiler at 2002: correct. Needs: its own 2002 verdict from this probe.

cases.reason: 2002's category-name list (11 words) is a subset of 2023's 13; 2023 adds FUNCTION-POINTER and MESSAGE-TAG, a widening. The rule asks only that no category word repeat, which depends on no operand's definition.

cases.reason: The format is the same. 2002 SR9 also admits communication-section items as identifier-3, but SR10 forbids only file or working-storage items of a factory or instance object. A CD item, which can exist only in a program definition, falls outside that ban in both readings, and admitting it is SR9's job, not SR10's. My probe at 2002: refute-p-14/inv-cd-rec.cob (INVOKE T 'BUMP' USING BY REFERENCE U1, where U1 is a CD record item) compiles and runs (U1=0008), so SR10 is not misapplied to it. Side finding for SR5c and 14.7, not this rule: refute-p-14/inv-cd-byref.cob passes the implicit CD name TL (an unsigned 4-digit integer per A.1.2.3 GR16b) BY REFERENCE to a PIC 9(4) formal, and the compiler refuses it with COBOL0828 'the argument is not [described with PICTURE 9(4)]'. That may be a conformance-matching defect for implicit descriptions.
